artifacts.note: Complete analysis output: density matrix, dominance pairs, ranking analysis, null control
Analysis script implementing 3-recipe OECD/COINr framework analysis
Source measurement data: 7 tasks, 3 definitions, locatable_sample capped at 20 elements

observations.description: The meta-analytic mean recipe (canonical + weighted)/2 always ranks EXACTLY between canonical and weighted on all 21 task-definition pairs. This is a mathematical certainty, not an empirical finding: for any x < y, (x+y)/2 satisfies x < (x+y)/2 < y.

All 3 pairwise dominance comparisons are strictly degenerate: canonical vs weighted = 0%, canonical vs mean = 0%, weighted vs mean = 100%. The meta-analytic mean introduces no new discrimination — it merely interpolates between the two existing recipes.

The 2-recipe degeneracy (all dominance 0%/100%) persists with 3 recipes. The degeneracy is NOT solely a 2-recipe artifact. The density metric itself lacks sufficient task-dependent recipe sensitivity to produce non-degenerate dominance with a linear combination recipe.

Null control (shuffling mean densities) produces ~2 non-degenerate pairs on average. Shuffling breaks the canonical<mean<weighted ordering, creating cases where the shuffled mean ranks outside the canonical-weighted range. The real mean never does this.

Canonical recipe produces near-zero densities (mean 0.006) because p=0.5 independent inclusion on a sparse locatable sample (20 elements) yields very low expected counts. Weighted recipe produces much higher densities (mean 0.195) because area-based weighting amplifies the signal from larger elements.

validity_notes.note: The meta-analytic mean is a LINEAR COMBINATION of the two existing recipes. For any two numbers x < y, (x+y)/2 always satisfies x < (x+y)/2 < y. This is a mathematical identity, not an empirical finding. The mean recipe can NEVER produce a non-degenerate dominance pair when the two original recipes have a strict ordering.

The 2-recipe degeneracy (0%/100% dominance) is a consequence of the density metric's extreme recipe sensitivity: canonical produces ~0.006, weighted produces ~0.195. These are 31x apart. The mean at ~0.101 is always between them. No linear combination can break this.

Results are bounded to truncated-first-20 locatable_sample (7 tasks, 1 site, 3 definitions). The density values are computed from capped data (20 elements per task, actual counts 21-82). Full DOM enumeration may change the density values but is unlikely to change the qualitative ranking structure.

A non-linear third recipe (e.g., DOM hierarchy depth, or a recipe that weights elements differently from both canonical and weighted) might produce rankings that sometimes fall outside the canonical-weighted range. This experiment tested only the simplest possible third recipe.

The frozen decision rule's C2 criterion (non-degenerate dominance >=1) is mathematically impossible to satisfy with a linear combination recipe when the two original recipes have strict ordering. This is a design limitation, not a measurement failure.
